issues.display_title: Issue #2078: feat(auth): email OTP (6-digit code) sign-in API
issues.main_description_html:
Background

Users can already sign in without a password through a magic link sent to their email (#2069), but that flow is for the website: the link opens a dashboard page in the browser. The desktop and mobile apps can't take over from a link opened in the browser, so they need a code the user types into the app instead.

Goal

Users with a GoThru account can sign in to the desktop and mobile apps with a 6-digit code sent to their email, without a password. The magic link stays the passwordless option for the website.

Scope

  • POST /v1/auth/otp: sends a 6-digit sign-in code to the email.
    • An unregistered email gets 404; a blocked account is rejected.
    • The code is valid for 15 minutes and can only be used once. Requesting a new code cancels the previous one.
    • Limits: one request per email per 60 seconds, and at most 5 requests per email per hour (separate from the magic link limits).
    • The response returns expires_in and resend_in so the app can show a countdown.
  • POST /v1/auth/otp/verify: checks email + code and logs the user in.
    • Returns the same response as the other logins (token + session cookie).
    • After 5 wrong codes the code is cancelled and the user must request a new one.
    • An unverified account is activated, since knowing the code proves the user owns the email.
    • A blocked account is rejected.
  • Only a hash of the code is stored; the code is never logged.
  • The email is sent with a Plunk template, with these variables: otp_code, expires_in_minutes.

Out of Scope

  • Designing the email template and its wording (#2079).
  • Desktop and mobile app screens for entering the code (separate tasks per app).
  • Using the code on the website (the website keeps the magic link).
  • Registering new accounts by code.
  • Per-IP limits (the API doesn't read the real client IP behind the proxy yet).

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: A registered email gets an email with a 6-digit code; the response is 200 with expires_in and resend_in.
  • AC-002: An unregistered email gets 404 and no email is sent. A blocked account gets 422. If the email can't be sent, the response is 503 and the user can try again straight away.
  • AC-003: A second request within 60 seconds, or a 6th within an hour, is rejected (429).
  • AC-004: A correct code logs the user in and returns the token + session cookie.
  • AC-005: A code that is wrong, expired (over 15 minutes), already used, or replaced by a newer code is rejected (401).
  • AC-006: After 5 wrong codes the next attempt is rejected (429), and even the correct code no longer works until a new one is requested.
  • AC-007: An unverified account is activated when the code is verified; a blocked account is rejected (422).
  • AC-008: Unit tests cover AC-001 – AC-007.

Dependencies

  • Email template (#2079): its UID 6c471406-68a1-4ba8-9878-ce346c9d298a is set in EmailTemplateUID::LOGIN_OTP (commit 5aaf43872, PR #2077).

Related

  • #2069: magic link sign-in API
  • #2077: this feature's PR

Result

Implementation

  • PR: #2077 (merged into main 2026-10-22, bee7c7cb1). It's shared with #2079, the email template.
  • Commits:
    • c9859e2a0 feat(auth): add 6-digit email OTP login (POST /v1/auth/otp, /otp/verify)
    • 5aaf43872 feat(email): set Plunk template ID for login OTP email (#2079)
    • 0dea174a2 feat(auth): extend login OTP expiry to 15 minutes (#2078)
  • POST /v1/auth/otp: emails a 6-digit code (15 min TTL, single use; a new request cancels the previous code). Returns { expires_in: 900, resend_in: 60 }. Only sha256(email|code) is stored in Redis (login_otp:* keys); the code is never logged.
  • POST /v1/auth/otp/verify: exchanges email + code for a GT token + session cookie, the same response shape as /auth/login. After 5 wrong codes the code is cancelled.
  • Per-email limits: 60s cooldown, max 5 requests per hour (separate from the magic link limits).
  • Error responses: 404 unregistered email, 422 blocked account, 429 over the limit / too many wrong codes, 401 invalid / expired / used / replaced code, 503 email send failure (code dropped and cooldown released so the user can retry right away).
  • Email template (#2079): EmailTemplateUID::LOGIN_OTP = 6c471406-68a1-4ba8-9878-ce346c9d298a. The API sends only otp_code and expires_in_minutes.
  • Unit tests: OtpRequestActionTest, OtpVerifyActionTest, OtpCodeRepositoryTest, EmailTemplateUIDTest.
  • API collection: Auth/OTP Request and Auth/OTP Verify (api-collection/GoThru API NEW/Auth/).

Testing

  • E2E test by the developer: passed. All acceptance criteria AC-001 – AC-008 passed.

Follow-ups (not blocking)

  • No daily cap on wrong codes per email: with 5 tries per code and 5 codes per hour, about 600 guesses per day are possible. A daily lockout would close this.
  • All limits are keyed by email only, so someone who knows a user's email can use up that user's attempts and requests.

Deploy status: not on production yet. The Jenkins deploy is blocked by a Jenkins server issue, so the merge hasn't been deployed.

issues.display_title: Issue #2079: feat(email): email OTP sign-in code template
issues.main_description_html:
Background

The email OTP sign-in API (#2078) sends users a 6-digit code they type into the app to sign in. The email needs a template in Plunk.

Goal

Users receive a clear email with their sign-in code that is easy to read and copy, and that tells them what to do if they didn't request it.

Scope

  • Template in Plunk (type Transactional, so the email reaches unsubscribed contacts and has no unsubscribe footer), in the same style as the existing GoThru emails (e.g. the magic link email, #2070).
  • Plunk template ID: 6c471406-68a1-4ba8-9878-ce346c9d298a
  • Variables used by the template:
    • otp_code: the 6-digit code, shown large in a box. The gaps between the digits come from CSS letter-spacing only, so copying it gives 387886, not 3 8 7 8 8 6.
    • expires_in_minutes: how long the code is valid (currently 15)
  • No "Copy code" button: email clients strip JavaScript, so it can't copy. Gmail and Apple Mail show their own copy option for codes.
  • Put the template ID into EmailTemplateUID::LOGIN_OTP in the API (on the #2078 branch, PR #2077), replacing the TODO-LOGIN-OTP-TEMPLATE-UID placeholder.

Wording

Subject: Your GoThru sign-in code

Your emergency sign-in code

Enter this code in Photo Studio to sign in:

[ {{otp_code}} ]

This single-use code expires in {{expires_in_minutes}} minutes.

Important: Never share this code. If you did not request it, you can safely ignore this email.

Need help? Reply to this message or contact support@gothru.co.

Best regards,
Alin Bugeag
CEO & Founder, GoThru Media Inc.
50 Halsey Ave, Toronto, ON, Canada

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: The template exists in Plunk (Transactional) and uses otp_code and expires_in_minutes.
  • AC-002: The wording is approved.
  • AC-003: The template ID is set in EmailTemplateUID::LOGIN_OTP.
  • AC-004: A test email arrives with the correct 6-digit code and expiry time, and copying the code gives the 6 digits with no spaces.

Related

  • #2078: email OTP sign-in API (PR #2077)
  • #2070: magic link email template

Result

Implementation

  • PR: #2077 (merged into main 2026-10-22, bee7c7cb1). It's shared with #2078, the email OTP API.
  • Key commit: 5aaf43872 feat(email): set Plunk template ID for login OTP email (#2079)
  • Plunk template created: type Transactional, ID 6c471406-68a1-4ba8-9878-ce346c9d298a.
  • EmailTemplateUID::LOGIN_OTP now holds the template ID. It's also registered in getAllUIDs() and in the name mapping under login-otp (getUIDByName() / getNameByUID()).
  • OtpRequestAction sends only otp_code and expires_in_minutes (currently 15); email and year were dropped since the template doesn't use them.
  • Expiry changed from 10 to 15 minutes in commit 0dea174a2; the template shows it through {{expires_in_minutes}}.

Testing

  • E2E test by the developer: passed. The email arrived from the new template with the 6-digit code and the 15-minute expiry. All acceptance criteria AC-001 – AC-004 passed.

Deploy status: not on production yet. The Jenkins deploy is blocked by a Jenkins server issue, so the merge hasn't been deployed.

issues.display_title: Issue #2084: fix(centering-tool): "Failed to get image dimensions" for panorama 47842960
issues.main_description_html:
Problem Description

Users report an error when centering/rotating a panorama in the moderator (centering tool API, CenteringTool::execute):

Failed to get image dimensions for panorama ID: 47842960 (file may be corrupted or invalid image format)

The error is thrown in RollImageClass::rollPanoImage(). The full image path is not empty, the file exists and is readable, but HelperClass::getImageDimensions() returns false.

Panorama

  • Pano ID: 47842960
  • Moderation / user: TBD (from the server log line RollImageClass::rollPanoImage - FAILED to get image dimensions. PanoId: 47842960 ...)

Notes

  • getImageDimensions() runs /usr/bin/identify -format "%w %h" <file> 2>&1 and discards ImageMagick's output on failure, so the real reason is not logged.
  • This failed before with getimagesize() too. Retries were added (36d7a29b8), then it was switched to identify (f835f675c). Neither fixed it.
  • Possible causes:
    • the file is corrupted, truncated, or not a JPEG
    • the pano_rotate worker is still rewriting the same file from a previous rotation
    • ImageMagick policy.xml width/area limits block large panoramas
  • Side effect: with rotate_all, fixAnglesForOnePano() runs before rollPanoImage(). A pano that fails here still gets its new fov saved to the DB, even though its image was never rotated.

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: Root cause for pano 47842960 identified with evidence (file info, identify output, server log).
  • AC-002: getImageDimensions() logs the real ImageMagick error when it fails.
  • AC-003: Fix applied (code or data). If it's data only (e.g. a broken file), document what's needed to recover it.

Result

Root cause (confirmed by a production test on 2026-10-23)

  • HelperClass::getImageDimensions() ran identify without -ping, so ImageMagick decoded the whole panorama just to read its width. On production that decode fails for panoramas of roughly 50 MP and up (the limit is between 32 MP and 50 MP). The function then returned false, and RollImageClass::rollPanoImage() threw "Failed to get image dimensions". Panorama 47842960 is 11904 × 5952 (70.9 MP).
  • The file is a valid JPEG. Metadata, JPEG type, the user and the tour play no role. It looked user-specific because only users with high-resolution panoramas are affected.
  • The old code also dropped ImageMagick's error message, so the cause never showed up in the logs.

Production test (regular account, new tour, current production code, synthetic panoramas with the same JPEG spec: baseline, q95, 4:2:0, XMP GPano)

Panorama Pixels Result
5760 × 2880 16.6 MP ✅
8000 × 4000 32.0 MP ✅
10000 × 5000 50.0 MP ❌ same error
11904 × 5952 (same spec, progressive, low detail, no metadata) 70.9 MP ❌ same error, all four
13600 × 6800 92.5 MP ❌ same error
16384 × 8192 134.2 MP ❌ same error

Implementation

  • Branch: fix/centering-image-dimensions-2084 (pushed, no PR yet).
  • Commits:
    • b509bd88a fix(helper): read image dimensions from header and log identify errors (#2084)
    • 2e1297d53 docs(investigations): centering tool image dimensions root cause and mitigation (#2084)
  • getImageDimensions():
    • identify -ping: reads the header only, so there is no decode and no size limit (on the devbox, a 70.9 MP panorama drops from ~558 MB / ~650 ms to ~11 MB / ~10 ms).
    • stdout and stderr are read separately, so ImageMagick warnings can't be parsed as the result.
    • A result is accepted only when the exit code is 0 and width and height are > 0.
    • Failures are logged with Log::warning('[HelperClass::getImageDimensions] identify failed', [...]), including path, file_size, exit_code, output and ImageMagick's error.
  • Unit tests: tests/Class/HelperClassGetImageDimensionsTest.php, not run yet.
  • Investigation doc: docs/investigations/2026-10-23-centering-tool-image-dimensions.md

Acceptance criteria status

  • AC-001: done (root cause with production evidence, see above).
  • AC-002: implemented in b509bd88a, not deployed.
  • AC-003: fix committed, not merged or deployed.

Follow-ups

  • After deploy, re-test the 50 MP+ panoramas and check that the image is actually rotated (thumbnail and version change). The pano_rotate worker also decodes the full image, so if it has a similar limit, the API would accept the request but the rotation would not happen.
  • DevOps: run identify -list resource, free -m and df -h /tmp on the API and worker servers to get the exact limit.
  • Dashboard Centering.jsx: the modal stays stuck in loading when version polling times out after 5 s.
  • rotate_all: call rollPanoImage() before fixAnglesForOnePano().

Deploy status: not merged, not on production.
